findings.title: Phase 10-07 execution blocked by UNBOUND phone client stack in CLIENT-BRANCHES.md
findings.description: Task 2 of 10-07-PLAN.md modifies apps/phone/src/pairing.tsx, apps/phone/src/sync.test.ts, apps/android-host/.../Pairing.kt and notes: 'Before execution rebind frontmatter and task file/check lists to only the D-056 owner-approved phone branch from CLIENT-BRANCHES.md... If phone branch is UNBOUND, retain BLOCKED status.' Per CLIENT-BRANCHES.md, the phone client status is currently 'UNBOUND. Neither phone client branch is currently locked. Physical experiment E3 must occur on physical hardware... before Phase 05/D-056 locks a branch.' Phase 10-07 cannot execute until Phase 05 E3 resolves the client branch. In addition, the automated verification command runs only Go and Swift Mac tests (rtk go test ./internal/space ./internal/host ./cmd/lumen ... && rtk swift test --package-path apps/mac-node --filter IdentityTests), omitting phone and Android test verification entirely despite listing phone files in files_modified.
findings.action: Rebind 10-07-PLAN.md frontmatter, task files, and verification commands only after Phase 05 E3 locks the phone client branch. Ensure that the verification command executes the test suite for the selected client branch (e.g. npm --prefix apps/phone test or ./gradlew :apps:android-host:test).

findings.title: Plan declares autonomous: false without containing any checkpoint or human-gated task
findings.description: 10-04-PLAN.md declares autonomous: false in its YAML frontmatter, yet its sole task is an automated tracer task (<task type="tracer" tdd="true">). It contains no checkpoint task (<task type="checkpoint:..." or gate="blocking-human"). In GSD workflow execution, autonomous: false signals an interactive or human-gated plan requiring user interaction; when no checkpoint task exists, automated runner harnesses halt unexpectedly or misroute task dispatch. The same defect occurs in 10-06-PLAN.md:8 (two auto tasks), 10-07-PLAN.md:8 (two auto tasks), 10-08-PLAN.md:8 (one auto task), 12-02-PLAN.md:19 (four auto tasks), 13-05-PLAN.md:8 (two auto tasks), and 14-02-PLAN.md:14 (one auto task).
findings.action: For plans whose prerequisites are satisfied by prior waves (10-04, 10-06, 10-08), set autonomous: true. For plans that conditionally wait on an owner decision or rebind (10-07, 12-02, 13-05, 14-02), either add an explicit <task type="checkpoint:decision" gate="blocking-human"> task with defined resume-signal or set autonomous: true if gating is handled entirely by the preceding plan.

findings.title: Mid-plan blocking human decision checkpoint precedes automated code task within the same wave
findings.description: In 12-01-PLAN.md, Task 3 (lines 55-64) is defined as <task type="checkpoint:decision" gate="blocking-human"><name>12-01 decision gate</name>, requiring the owner to select between native EventKit or Hermes skill. However, Task 4 (lines 65-73) is an automated code task (<task type="auto"><name>12-01: Freeze Host action reducer</name>), which modifies internal/space/reminder.go and reads 12-01-EVIDENCE.md. Placing an automated implementation task after a blocking human checkpoint inside the same plan breaks wave-level batch execution, as autonomous runners cannot complete the plan's code modifications without manual intervention midway through the plan.
findings.action: Move Task 4 ('Freeze Host action reducer') before Task 3, or split the human decision gate into a dedicated final checkpoint task of 12-01-PLAN.md (or a wave 1 exit gate) so that all code modifications in 12-01 complete before pausing for the human decision.

findings.title: Physical hardware testing and accessibility verification embedded in autonomous plans without human checkpoints
findings.description: Both 09-01-PLAN.md and 09-02-PLAN.md are marked autonomous: true, but their task actions require physical hardware tests: 09-01 requires physical Android desk voice capture via microphone, physical wake word, Mac node action, and live provider validation; 09-02 requires physical screen reader (TalkBack/VoiceOver), keyboard navigation, dynamic text scaling, and display rotation on actual devices. Furthermore, 09-01 allows marking evidence BLOCKED if hardware is missing while the automated check passes, allowing an autonomous executor to mark the phase done without actual physical multi-device validation.
findings.action: Add explicit <task type="checkpoint:human-verify" gate="blocking-human"> to 09-01-PLAN.md and 09-02-PLAN.md requiring physical device confirmation before phase exit, and set autonomous: false on plans requiring physical hardware interaction.

findings.title: Stale plan references in Phase 10 source review cite superseded plan numbering
findings.description: Lines 22-25 of 10-SOURCE-REVIEW.md state: '## 10-05 ... Seven-day soak and owner sign-off are explicit (10-05-PLAN.md:20-21); preserve BLOCKED status until actual elapsed duration and named physical acceptance exist.' However, Phase 10 was subsequently expanded from 5 plans to 9 plans; 10-05-PLAN.md is now the transfer/quarantine plan, while the seven-day soak and owner sign-off tasks reside in 10-09-PLAN.md:20-21.
findings.action: Update line 24 of 10-SOURCE-REVIEW.md to reference 10-09-PLAN.md:20-21 instead of 10-05-PLAN.md:20-21.

findings.title: Requirement frontmatter omits FR-39 mapping while tasks implement FR-39 facet reconciliation
findings.description: In 13-01-PLAN.md, frontmatter specifies requirements: [] (empty list), yet Task 1 (13-01: Reconcile FR-39 facet evidence) explicitly claims to reconcile FR-39 facet evidence across the existing codebase. Similarly, 13-05-PLAN.md specifies requirements: [] despite implementing certified Hermes skill and MCP facets directly addressing FR-39 ('Hermes skill and MCP execution with Host grants'). While 14-05-PLAN.md owns final FR-39 closure, the intermediate contributor plans in Phase 13 should either document their facet contribution or note that FR-39 remains open until 14-05.
findings.action: Add an explanatory note in 13-01 and 13-05 frontmatter clarifying that FR-39 is owned by Phase 14 (14-05-PLAN.md) while 13-01 and 13-05 prepare the non-canonical facet evidence and typed seams.

findings.title: Automated check verifies Go setup runner but omits syntax and lint validation of install.sh
findings.description: In 15-03-PLAN.md, Task 1 creates and modifies install.sh (the primary one-command bootstrap installer), internal/setup/runner.go, and cmd/lumen-setup/main.go. However, <verify><automated> executes only rtk go test ./internal/setup ./cmd/lumen-setup -count=1. It does not execute shellcheck install.sh or run bash -n install.sh, meaning syntax errors, shell parameter bugs, or portable POSIX incompatibilities in install.sh will not fail the automated gate.
findings.action: Update <verify><automated> in 15-03-PLAN.md to include shellcheck install.sh or bash -n install.sh alongside the Go tests.

findings.title: Automated check runs npm check but does not verify Go embed build dependency for cmd/lumen-managed
findings.description: In 16-05-PLAN.md, Task 1 modifies apps/managed-web/src/... and cmd/lumen-managed/web.go. The Go binary embeds web assets via //go:embed web/dist/*. The verification command is rtk go test ./internal/managed -count=1 && rtk npm --prefix apps/managed-web run check. npm run check typically runs TypeScript and ESLint, but does not execute npm run build to generate apps/managed-web/dist. As a result, compiling cmd/lumen-managed or running integration tests embedding those assets will fail or test stale assets if a build step is not run.
findings.action: Update <verify><automated> in 16-05-PLAN.md to run rtk npm --prefix apps/managed-web run build and rtk go build ./cmd/lumen-managed to prove that the embedded web distribution compiles cleanly into the Go binary.

findings.title: DST fold and ambiguous timezone recovery requires explicit clock jump test
findings.description: Task 1 of 14-04-PLAN.md specifies handling DST fold/gap and clock steps using occurrence keys (schedule, version, nominal UTC). While the behavior describes DST handling, the automated test command (rtk go test ./internal/automation ./internal/host ./internal/store -count=1) does not explicitly test backward clock adjustments (NTP steps backward) or monotonic lease expiry across system clock jumps, relying on standard time packages which may use wall clock rather than monotonic clock for lease durations.
findings.action: Explicitly require a negative test in internal/automation that simulates a backward system clock jump of at least 1 hour and asserts that active leases do not extend and duplicate occurrences are not dispatched.

findings.title: Scoped member export and restore depends on uncommitted 17-05 matrix
findings.description: Tasks 17-08b and 17-08c state: 'BLOCKED until the approved 17-05 matrix determines export recipients and member restore destination.' 17-05 produces SHARED-SPACE-THREAT-MODEL.md. Because the role-scoped export format (FR-77/FR-78) distinguishes full owner backup from member export, if 17-05 does not define exact field-level redaction rules for each non-owner role, 17-08 will be forced to invent redaction policies during execution.
findings.action: Ensure 17-05-PLAN.md explicit checklist includes field-by-field redaction rules for member export envelopes prior to 17-08 execution.

blockers: 10-07-PLAN.md is blocked because the phone client branch in CLIENT-BRANCHES.md is UNBOUND pending physical experiment E3; Task 2 cannot execute or be verified until Phase 05/D-056 is locked.

Seven execution plans (10-04, 10-06, 10-07, 10-08, 12-02, 13-05, 14-02) declare autonomous: false without containing any checkpoint task (<task type="checkpoint:..." or gate="blocking-human"), halting automated GSD runners unexpectedly.
12-01-PLAN.md sequences a blocking human decision checkpoint (Task 3) before an automated code implementation task (Task 4) within the same plan, breaking automated wave completion.

09-01-PLAN.md and 09-02-PLAN.md embed physical hardware testing (microphone, wake word, Mac node, mobile accessibility) inside autonomous: true plans without blocking human verification checkpoints, allowing unverified phase completion.
